title: Colonel Gardine sends him to the old post in the bushes
summary: The Colonel visited the field camp, picked Procope and told him he'd be sent to the old post, free to take others, but his comrades wanted to stick together.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So, getting back, Colonel Gardine -- now, imagine, to show you how tight our outfit were, we were in a clearing. You know, we'd get up in the morning and build a fire and sit around the fire, in the winter, cold you know. So I saw these bushes, and lo and behold here comes the Colonel, Colonel Gardine. You know, he made out like it was an official visit. So everybody jumped up and stood at attention. He said, "As you were. At ease." He says, "Where's --," What was the Captain's name? "Where's Captain Barry --," I think it was. "Where's Captain Barry?" Said, "I don't know, sir, he was around here a little while ago. But I think he'll be back. I think he just went down to the first aid tent or something like that. So he looked at me and he said, "Come here. You'll do." I said, "He come to get the Colonel, and I'll do?" Anyway, I went with him. So the Colonel said to me, he says, "Have you heard from the old post?" I said, "No." He said, "Well, you will." He said, "I'm sending you up to the old post. You don't have to go overseas." And he says, "Anybody you want to take with you, just let me know and you can take them with you." How's that for a two-striper?

So he said, 'Well, you'll hear from them.' Then he left. So I went -- I was so happy, I told some of the fellows sitting around, I said, 'The Colonel's going to transfer me up to the old post, with the band.' I said, 'Any of you fellows want to go with me? You can if you want to, you know.' And I remember one fellow spoke up and said, 'No, we want to stick together.' I said, 'Okay, forget it.' And I turned my back and I left. And a couple of days later, here comes a fellow in a station wagon, took me and all my gear and everything. There was one other fellow the Colonel sent with me. He was a fellow who was a drummer in the band, you know, so it wouldn't look like -- he sent the two of us. I think this other fellow was a Sergeant or something. He said the tour was up to the old post.
